title: Textplot
subtitle: Small charts inside your query results.
intro: Render a numeric sequence or progress value as terminal-friendly text. Keep the underlying values for sorting and computation; add plots as a compact visual summary.

reference.name: tp_bar(value, ...)
reference.description: Render one value against a configured range.

reference.name: tp_sparkline(values, ...)
reference.description: Render a DOUBLE list as a compact sequence.

reference.name: tp_density(values, ...)
reference.description: Render the distribution of a DOUBLE list.

reference.name: tp_qr(text, ...)
reference.description: Render text as an ASCII or Unicode QR code.

reference.name: width := n
reference.description: Control chart width with a named argument.

reference.name: array_agg(value ORDER BY time)
reference.description: Build an ordered sequence before rendering a sparkline.

notes.title: Match the terminal
notes.body: Use ASCII styles where Unicode width or emoji rendering is unreliable. Dense characters can look different across terminal fonts and exported logs.

notes.title: A picture is a string
notes.body: Plot functions return VARCHAR. Aggregate and order the numeric data before plotting; sort results on the numbers, not on the rendered bars.

examples.title: An ASCII progress bar
examples.caption: Quote reserved named arguments such as on and off.

examples.title: A sequence & a distribution
examples.caption: Sparklines preserve sequence; density summarizes the distribution.

examples.title: Aggregate in order
examples.caption: Use ORDER BY inside array_agg so chronology is explicit.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN typeof(tp_bar(0.7))='VARCHAR' AND length(tp_sparkline([1,2,3]))>0 THEN true ELSE error('plot output') END;
